A colossal clay waterfall thunders down a sheer ochre cliff-face, white frothy clay spray billowing into a churning gorge below — so enormous the toy dinos clustered at its base look like specks.

A sky-high clay mesa dominates the entire backdrop, its flat-topped silhouette banded in rust, ochre, and cream clay strata, sheer vertical walls dropping hundreds of scale-feet to dusty canyon floor.
A titanic clay glacier wall looms across the background, pale blue and white clay layered in deep crevasse cracks, a massive ice-shelf calving a huge frozen clay chunk into grey meltwater below.

An enormous clay crystal spire field erupts from the earth, translucent tinted clay pillars soaring skyward in jagged clusters, the tallest central spire dwarfing every dinosaur figure posed around its base.

A monstrous clay meteor streaks down from the upper frame, trailing a thick spiralling clay smoke plume, its glowing orange clay nose aimed at a fresh smouldering crater already punched into the ground.
A vast tar-pit lake of black glossy clay stretches across the background, a half-submerged colossal clay skeleton rising from its centre, ribs and skull breaking the surface like a drowning giant.
A towering clay geyser erupts a roaring column of white clay water and steam straight up into the sky, the pillar wider than three toy dinos standing side by side, misting the whole scene.

A colossal fallen clay log spans the entire width of the frame, its bark textured in ridged brown clay, moss-green clay patches clinging to its surface, dinosaur figures dwarfed beneath its vast curved belly.

A mammoth clay storm-wall blackens the background sky, dark grey and violet clay clouds boiling forward, jagged white clay lightning bolts forking downward, the advancing tempest making every dino in the foreground look minuscule.
A gigantic clay rock arch soars across the background, its legs planted wide on either side of the scene, rust-red clay banding visible in its curve, toy dinos walking beneath it like ants.

An enormous clay amber-resin tree dominates the backdrop, its trunk wider than the whole diorama floor, golden clay sap oozing in thick glossy rivulets down the deeply textured bark, roots erupting from the earth.

A colossal clay terraced cascade waterfall steps down a cliff in five massive tiers, each shelf thundering white clay water into the next broad pool, rainbow clay mist rising from the thundering lowest basin.

A sky-piercing clay crystal monolith — single, impossibly tall, deep violet clay shot through with white veins — rises dead-centre in the background, its tip lost in clay cloud wisps far above the scene.
A titanic clay gorge splits the background open, sheer terracotta clay walls plunging to a barely-visible river of blue clay far below, the scale so vast the dinosaurs at the rim look like toys.

A massive clay geyser field fills the background with a dozen erupting clay vents, one central monster-geyser blasting a thick white clay column triple the height of any other feature in the entire diorama.

An enormous erupting clay volcano anchors the far background, a lava fountain of red-orange clay arcing overhead and a billowing grey clay mushroom-cloud rolling skyward, toy dinos at the base utterly dwarfed by its mass.

A colossal clay iceberg rises from a frozen clay sea, its above-water peak jagged and white-blue, deep translucent teal clay submerged bulk visible beneath the surface, fissures and cracks carved dramatically across its massive face.

A giant clay skeleton of a long-necked sauropod lies fossilised in a cliff-face, each bone individually sculpted in pale clay, the skull alone wider than several toy dinos, its ribcage forming a cavernous hollow.

A towering clay hoodoo forest fills the background — dozens of mushroom-cap clay pillars in red and orange, the tallest central spire soaring far above the rest, toy dinos clustered at its crumbling base.

A vast clay lava plain stretches back to a distant horizon, cracked black clay crust glowing orange-red in deep fissures, a slow churning clay lava river snaking forward, the sheer scale reducing all dinos to specks.

A monumental clay cliff-face carved by ancient rivers rises sheer across the entire background, horizontal clay strata in deep reds, purples, and yellows, a thin clay waterfall thread dropping its full height into the scene.

An enormous clay sinkhole yawns open centre-background, its circular clay rim crumbling at the edges, the interior dropping into impenetrable shadow, steam rising from below, surrounding dinos peering over the edge looking impossibly small.

A colossal clay geothermal mud-pool boils and burbles across the background, fat clay bubble-domes swelling and popping on its surface, sulphur-yellow clay mineral deposits ringing its banks, the whole feature dominating the diorama horizon.

A titanic clay natural dam of piled boulders spans the background, behind it a vast deep-blue clay lake stretching to far clay mountains, the dam's crest towering above the foreground dinosaurs like a wall.

A sky-high clay canyon wall fills the backdrop entirely, its face honeycombed with eroded clay caves at every level, a thin clay river glinting at its base, the sheer vertical scale making all dinos microscopic.
